# osmunda

The Lentago Labs **Kubernetes platform** — everything above the nodes. A standing
**k3s** cluster on the lab's own LXC guests is the default home for workloads; an
**ephemeral EKS overlay** is stood up and torn down per task when a job genuinely
needs cloud Kubernetes. Everything is reconciled **pull-based via [Flux](https://fluxcd.io)**:
the controllers run *inside* the cluster and pull desired state from this repo —
CI validates manifests, it never deploys them. The first workload migrating in is
**n8n** (from LXC 113).

**Authorship:** The manifests, documentation, and configuration in this repo are
co-written with [Claude](https://claude.ai) (Anthropic). I direct the work and
review the output; Claude writes the YAML and prose. I'm an infrastructure
operator, not a software engineer — please don't read this repo as a portfolio
of coding ability.

## 🧭 What this repo is

osmunda sits **above the nodes**. Node provisioning and the k3s install live
elsewhere (in *kalmia*); this repo owns the platform: what runs on the clusters
and how it gets there.

| Layer | Shape |
|---|---|
| **Standing cluster** | k3s on the lab's LXC guests — `k3s-1` (pve5), `k3s-2` (pve4). Always on, zero standing cloud cost. |
| **Cloud overlay** | Ephemeral EKS, created for a specific task and **torn down immediately**. Control plane bills **~$0.10/h** while it exists — a deliberately flagged exception to free-tier-first. |
| **GitOps** | Pull-based via Flux. Controllers reconcile in-cluster from `clusters/`; CI does not deploy. |
| **Workload identity** | Continues the fleet's OIDC thesis — IRSA on the EKS side. |
| **First workload** | n8n, migrating off LXC 113. Manifests in `apps/n8n/` are a **pre-cutover draft**. |

Why it's built this way is recorded in the ADRs, framed as fit-for-this-lab
choices rather than claims about the better tool:

- [ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-k3s-lab-plus-ephemeral-eks.md) — k3s on the lab, EKS only when ephemeral (cost sovereignty).
- [ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-flux-over-argocd.md) — Flux for GitOps (lighter footprint for a 2-node lab; reconcilers match the pull-not-push thesis).

## 🗺️ Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`clusters/lab/`](clusters/lab/) | Flux entrypoint for the standing k3s cluster: `flux-system/` bootstrap placeholder + `Kustomization`s (infra → apps) |
| [`clusters/eks-ephemeral/`](clusters/eks-ephemeral/) | Overlay skeleton for the on-demand EKS cluster |
| [`apps/n8n/`](apps/n8n/) | n8n Deployment / PVC / Service / Ingress — **pre-cutover draft** |
| [`infra/`](infra/) | Ingress controller + storage notes and the infrastructure reconcile target |
| [`runbooks/`](runbooks/) | [`eks-up.md`](runbooks/eks-up.md) / [`eks-down.md`](runbooks/eks-down.md) — stand-up / tear-down with the cost gate |
| [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/) | Architecture decision records |
| [`.github/workflows/kubeconform.yml`](.github/workflows/kubeconform.yml) | Validates every manifest under `apps/` + `clusters/` on each PR |

## ⛔ The cost gate

The one rule that is load-bearing: **the EKS control plane must never be left up
idle.** It bills ~$0.10/hour for as long as it exists — the single flagged
exception to the fleet's free-tier-first stance. The runbooks make standing it
up inseparable from tearing it down:

- [`runbooks/eks-up.md`](runbooks/eks-up.md) — stand up for a specific, time-boxed task.
- [`runbooks/eks-down.md`](runbooks/eks-down.md) — stop the meter the moment the task is done.

Durable state never lives on the ephemeral side; it stays on the lab or in a
managed service.

## 🛠️ How it works

- **Reconciliation is pull-based.** `flux bootstrap` installs the GitOps-toolkit
  controllers into the cluster and points them at `clusters/lab/`. They then
  reconcile `infrastructure.yaml` (ingress, storage) before `apps.yaml` (n8n, …)
  on an interval. Nothing is pushed from CI. See [`clusters/lab/README.md`](clusters/lab/README.md).
- **CI validates, it does not deploy.** [`kubeconform.yml`](.github/workflows/kubeconform.yml)
  runs on every PR and validates the manifests under `apps/` and `clusters/`
  against the Kubernetes schemas. Custom resources (Flux, kustomize) are skipped;
  core resources are checked strictly.
- **Images are digest-pinned.** e.g. n8n is pinned by `@sha256:…` so the deployed
  bits never drift from the reviewed ones.
